description:
FILED s464aw (found by a #972 guard-row probe; PRE-EXISTING -- identical on an
80b715c worktree, and it is why that guard's fixture is `bless {}').

    my $u = bless [], 'Plain';
    "$u"        both  Plain=ARRAY(0xâ¦)         <- stringification is fine
    $u x 2      perl  Plain=ARRAY(0x1)Plain=ARRAY(0x1)
                PCL   ""                        <- the reference is GONE

    package A; use overload q("") => sub {"AB"}; sub new { bless [], shift }
    A->new x 2  perl  ABAB     PCL  00

    # the other two payload kinds are correct:
    $hashref  x 2   both  the stringification twice
    $scalarref x 2  both  the stringification twice

So `x' with an ARRAY-payload box on the left is being treated as perl's LIST
repetition (`(LIST) x N') instead of string repetition: a box holding a
vector is a REFERENCE and `x' must stringify it.  perl decides list-vs-string
repetition SYNTACTICALLY (the left operand must be a parenthesised list or a
`qw'), never from the operand's runtime type.

The `00' in the overloaded case is the same thing seen through a `""'
handler: the empty array repeats to nothing and the surrounding numeric
coercion prints 0 twice.

SUSPECT: `p-str-x' (or the codegen that chooses between `p-str-x' and a
list-repeat form) branches on the operand's payload being a vector.  The
discriminating measurement is one `./pl2cl' of `my $r=[]; print $r x 2;' --
if the emitted form is already the list-repeat one the bug is in the codegen,
if it is `p-str-x' it is in the runtime.

BAR: the six rows above vs perl; the layer's own bar (corpus-diff if codegen,
the sweep either way); a guard row.
subject: $aryref x N is LIST repetition -- the reference is lost (blessed or not)
